acceptanceJudgements.criterion: Timeouts, corrupted/replayed results and interrupted jobs never become passed/accepted
acceptanceJudgements.judgement: approved-at-protocol-level (tested on the synthetic runtime; no real VM)
evidence: store.ts recordResult re-verifies every delivered result with packages/runner-protocol verifyTrustedResult against the row-rebuilt Job/Lease (no signing reimplementation); any unauthenticated/binding-mismatch/stale/malformed/incomplete/contradictory outcome is recorded as an unverified evidence row and completes the job unverified with evaluation -> infrastructure_failure (applyAnomaly, store.ts:444-458)
runner-declared unverified: applyRunnerUnverified records class unverified + cause 'runner_reported_unverified', never passing (store.ts:461-467)

replay: bounded canonical payload digest of the delivered signed input; payloadSeenBefore marks duplicates 'replayed_result' (store.ts:118-129,400-403); verified pass retains authority and replay cannot overturn it (fixture scenario 1: authoritative_outcome stays 'passed', evaluation stays public_evaluating)

late/post-cancel/post-completion results: recorded unverified 'late_result', never affecting state (store.ts:317-320); past-deadline delivery throws 'Stale runner result.' -> stale_result -> infrastructure_failure

log bytes that mismatch the signed logDigest downgrade a verified claim to unverified 'log_mismatch' (store.ts:324); stored logs are first-capture-wins (captureLogs ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) and digest-bound to the stored bytes

timeouts/interruptions: recordTimeout valid on running only (queued 422), recordInterruption validates the cause enum; both insert infrastructure evidence and land evaluation in infrastructure_failure; terminal reports are honest no-ops (recorded:false)

DDL defense-in-depth: class/outcome alignment CHECK, authoritative_result_required matching against the append-only results table, result rows UPDATE/DELETE-raising triggers, log rows immutable except delete under a cancelled parent, jobs binding fields row-immutability trigger, 1 MiB bytea bound (ddl.ts + migration 0007); sql-guards fixture scenario asserts exact SQL error messages for binding mutation, idle version bump, result/log tamper, oversized log insert

aggregate rule: aggregateAuthoritativeOutcome requires verified passing evidence for BOTH kinds; infrastructure -> infrastructure_failure; any unverified -> unverified; public-only/private-only -> unverified (never passed); buildInternalEvaluationResult throws EvaluationNotPassedError otherwise; fixture scenario 'anomalies-never-pass' asserts evaluation state infrastructure_failure and result payload null for corrupt/forged/log-mismatch/runner-unverified/malformed/past-deadline cases
acceptanceJudgements.limitation: exercised against the isolated synthetic PostgreSQL fixture inside the synthetic runtime; real hostile-code execution belongs to M5.2/M5.4 and remains blocked

acceptanceJudgements.criterion: Evidence binds evaluated bytes and revisions (digest bindings)
evidence: verifiedResultEvidence rejects any record whose packageHash/submissionHash/artifactHash/imageDigest/harnessId/harnessDigest/jobId/jobKind differ from the immutable job binding (runner-results/index.ts:161-187)

InternalEvaluationResult evidence entries bind checkId/jobId/jobKind/artifactHash/harnessDigest and the result binds evaluationId/attemptId/submissionHash/packageHash/privateBaseRevision; verified-flow fixture scenario asserts exact artifact linkage (ARTIFACT_PUBLIC vs ARTIFACT_PRIVATE) and revision hashes in the owner-review payload
trimCapture digest always names exactly the stored bytes with complete/originalByteCount provenance
verifyEvidenceBinding reports every drifted field including revision.taskId/taskVersion/privateBaseRevision

acceptanceJudgements.criterion: Job cleanup cannot affect another workspace or active job
evidence: cancel/cleanup operate inside one transaction scoped to a single FOR UPDATE job row, require evaluation.operator + in-transaction session re-validation (requiresEvaluationOperator) and exact expectedVersion (stale -> 409); cleanup deletes only the log row of that job and refuses completed jobs (store.ts:361-398)

cleanup-isolation fixture scenario: A's cancel+cleanup leaves workspace B fully intact (B's verified evidence and log bytes preserved, authoritative_outcome 'passed'), second cleanup idempotent, completed cleanup refused, stale-version cancel denied, replay after terminal recorded unverified
SQL-level log delete requires a cancelled parent (trigger job_log_delete_requires_cancelled_parent)

enqueue is transactional with in-transaction actor/session re-check; duplicate identical binding returns created:false with no evaluation version churn (fixture asserts version stays 2 and one row per kind); any binding difference is JobBindingConflict 409; concurrent private enqueues produce exactly one created winner under unique (evaluation_id, job_kind) + (permit_id, job_kind) with unique-violation retry (fixture idempotent scenario)

authority: enqueue takes package/submission/task/permit/submissionId only from the permit-bound private_evaluations row (never caller assertions); requires approved release manifest executionImageDigest, exact published publicChecks set for public kind, fixed trustedHarness digest matching, deadline inside (now, now+120s], rejects superseded/out-of-order (private-before-public) enqueues; authority scenario asserts zero jobs created from client assertions

fixture sql-guards scenario asserts exact PG error strings: job_binding_immutable (job_kind/artifact/image/attempt/checks/deadline), invalid_job_transition (job_state to completed, idle version bump), job_result_immutable, job_log_immutable, job_log_delete_requires_cancelled_parent, 23514 for a 1,048,577-byte log insert

independently traced the trigger: a completed row cannot be re-pointed at a fabricated authoritative result (sequence must reference an existing recorded row with equal class/outcome/cause), cannot leave completed, cannot resurrect cancelled
projectPublicFeedback exposes only approved categories and public-verified check details; private evidence contributes nothing; unknown states/ids/versions fail closed; forged categories rejected
store read projections carry digests only; readLogs is the only raw-log path and is operator-only with in-transaction session validation
projectJobError maps to fixed safe strings (403/409/422/503) and never leaks internal detail
layering probes: runner-results imports only contracts modules; the store import surface is allowlisted (no private-api internals)

acceptanceJudgements.criterion: Never-pass guarantee vs SECURITY.md ('Hostile submissions and isolated evaluator', 'Additional reviewed gates')
evidence: unsigned/corrupt/unavailable jobs become infrastructure/unverified rows, never acceptance (SECURITY.md line 27); the store completes only via authoritative evidence rows which are append-only and class-aligned

jobs cannot accept themselves: the highest state the store produces is owner_review with a verified-passed aggregate payload; acceptance remains M7 (owner-only), and M7 guidance in the draft records superseded/infrastructure/changes_required as never accepted
no gate in code or evidence claims real-VM validation; state.json M5.3 blockers state 'Protocol-level only: no real VM'; the M5.2 dedicated-Linux-KVM prerequisite is unchanged and blocked

retainedFailures: worker-disclosed mid-attempt failures: lifecycle-suite-final.json / lifecycle-suite-final2.json (byte-identity guard catching the initial hand-written migration copy) retained as unverified/exit 1; empty-migration-report.json reports foundation/intake/total counts honestly (22 total = 10 foundation + 5 intake + 7 release/job tables)
no new failing run was produced in this review; both rerun suites exited 0
limitations: All lifecycle/store observations ran against the isolated synthetic runtime databases; no real VM, no real hostile patch, no controller-to-store wiring exists yet (M5.4).

recordResult treats log bytes as optional today (M5.1 controller supplies only the signed result); when absent the signed logDigest is recorded as attestation without stored bytes - disclosed in the draft and accepted for M5.3 scope with capture wiring owned by M5.4.
artifact-digest authority is first-hash binding per (evaluation, kind) with image/harness enforced against approved release data - disclosed optional M5.4/M5.2 hardening; not a never-pass violation.

Cancellation mid-flight leaves the evaluation in operator-visible limbo (e.g. public_evaluating) rather than a synthetic failure state; the store never manufactures acceptance - disclosed, M5.4/M7 own recovery.
Read-only observation: idle version bumps on completed job rows are not rejected by the SQL trigger (app-level staleness already denies their use); defence-in-depth nitpick, no never-pass impact.
